content.text: I think it will be common that we have "upgrade" utilities from release to release.
Please create a new fcrepo4-labs repository that will hold these appropriately named utilities.
, are you working this? Or should
pick it up?
If the latter, please provide some more notes in this ticket on how you had envisioned this utility working to help with
's implementation.
If
can pick it up, that would be great – I don't expect to have time to work on it this week, but should have time next week if it's not wrapped up by then.

My expectation is that we would create a JAR package with dependencies bundled, so users could download a single runnable JAR file.  Operation would be by running the JAR file (optionally with the --dryrun parameter to just show what would be done).  We will need to pick up the repository configuration and should allow providing a custom configuration by System property like we do with the WAR artifacts.
: here's my branch:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-upgrade-utils

– it currently builds a JAR and pulls in most of the dependencies and Spring config, but doesn't pull in the core JCR classes, and I'm not sure how the Spring context should be setup (should we be running a Spring context loader, or update the class to explicitly load beans?)
Give this a shot,
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-upgrade-utils/pull/2
p.s. I would suggest changing the top-level package name from:
package org.fcrepo.utils
to:
package org.fcrepo.upgrade.utils

, I've merged #2 and moved the package to org.fcrepo.upgrade.utils.  I've also added the Spring machinery to load beans from the command-line.  This seems to be almost working, but fails with an error about not being able to load the namespace handler for the "p" namespace.  This looks like it's related to a bug in the maven assembly plugin, and people recommend different plugins (e.g., maven-shade-plugin):
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3335203/yet-another-unable-to-locate-spring-namespacehandler-error
I'm out of time to work on this, but I think it's very close.
Can you move this ticket to "Start Work" so it is on my radar?
, This PR gets you further... but additional error-handling is required when running it against an actual repository:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-upgrade-utils/pull/3

, I've updated fcrepo4-upgrade-utils to improve the error handling, remove some redundant logging, and use jcr:mimeType instead of fedora:mimeType.  I also added a call to session.save() so non-dryrun operation now actually updates the repository.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-upgrade-utils/commit/f238239e127c3e43c9760af4401deb36df839337
This now successfully migrates the metadata on files for me, and when I apply the PR 790 and the updated PR 791, newly-created files have the same properties as the migrated ones.
I assume the next steps for this will be to load a larger number of files and test running the migration at scale?

If you have a larger migration with which to test, that would be great. Once you have done that, please push this ticket into Review and we can hopefully include it in the release scheduled for the week of the 20th.

I have loaded 935K files in a local fcrepo 4.1.1 repository and run TechnicalMetadataMigrator to migrate the technical metadata properties.  It took about 53 minutes to process the files, at a rate of about 17K files/minute.  So I feel confident that the tool scales well to large numbers of files.
Update committed without PR.
Recent changes to 4.2-SNAPSHOT have changed the properties used to store technical metadata for files/NonRDFSources, such as the SHA-1 checksum, mime type, and file name:
fedora:digest => premis:hasMessageDigest
fedora:mimeType => ebucore:mimeType
premis:hasOriginalName => ebucore:filename
Develop a utility that will traverse a repository and migrate these properties.
